text:
Anaheim has now won three straight, and this one nearly slipped away. The Ducks led 5-2 early in the third period, then watched Edmonton score twice in the last four minutes, the second from Leon Draisaitl with 45 seconds left, before hanging on to win 5-4.

The goals came from the Ducks' defense and its young forwards. Pavel Mintyukov, a defenseman drafted 10th overall by Anaheim in 2022 out of Saginaw, scored twice in the second period, 63 seconds apart. Beckett Sennecke, the third pick in 2024, also scored twice and had an assist, one of them a power-play goal early in the third. Mintyukov was named the game's first star. Connor McDavid had a goal and three assists in a losing effort, including a short-handed goal on a chance we gave only a 2% chance of going in.

Our numbers say Edmonton played the better game. The Oilers took 57 shot attempts to 46 and won 34 of 52 faceoffs. Expected goals, our measure of chance quality, finished 3.58 to 3.51 for Edmonton, which gives the Oilers a slight edge (51%) in how often they would win if the game were replayed. Edmonton owned the third period, 1.56 to 0.71. Anaheim's lead was built in the second, when it out-chanced the Oilers 1.77 to 1.29. Matt Tomkins allowed about 1.5 goals more than the shots he faced should have produced, and that gap decided the game.

Anaheim carries a three-game winning streak out of Edmonton. The Oilers lost on home ice a month after beating the Ducks 5-2 on Oct. 7.
